_about: Sample questions come from RAG-Hands-On-Use-Cases.docx. That file gives no answers, so reference_answer, key_facts and expected_pages were written by reading the PDF text layer (pdftotext) of each report. Pages are 1-based PDF page indexes (what the app cites), not the numbers printed on the page. key_facts: every inner list must have at least one alternative present in the answer (case-insensitive) for the answer to pass.

questions.question: How many depository libraries did GPO staff visit in FY 2018?
questions.reference_answer: GPO staff visited 166 depository libraries in 25 states.

questions.question: What new digital system replaced FDsys, and when was it fully deployed?
questions.reference_answer: govinfo. It came out of beta in December 2017, ran in parallel with FDsys through 2018, and FDsys was scheduled to be completely retired and replaced by govinfo in December 2018.

questions.question: How much did GPO procure in printing and information products in FY 2018 on behalf of federal agencies?
questions.reference_answer: Approximately $375.7 million (84,111 orders); the Director's message rounds this to more than $375 million.

documents.title: World Bank Global Economic Prospects June 2026

questions.question: What is the growth outlook for South Asia in this report?
questions.reference_answer: Growth in SAR is expected to soften to 6.3 percent in 2026 (Middle East conflict: higher energy prices, reduced oil/gas supplies, disrupted remittances and tourism), then pick up to an average of 7 percent per year in 2027-28. India is projected to moderate to 6.6 percent in FY2026/27.

questions.question: What does Chapter 3 say about sovereign debt in developing economies?
questions.reference_answer: Rising government debt is a key EMDE challenge: it raises interest rates, debt-service payments and the likelihood of distress. Debt levels are positively and non-linearly associated with sovereign spreads and domestic yields; the rise in EMDE debt-to-GDP since 2010 is associated with increases of about 110 and 30 basis points. Effects are larger with a history of default, low ratings, frontier status, short-term debt reliance and weak governance. EMDE government debt rose from under 40 percent of GDP in 2010 to over 70 percent. Policy: strengthen fiscal positions (revenue mobilization, efficient spending, debt management, domestic debt markets, debt-for-development swaps).

questions.question: According to the executive summary, what are the main risks to the global outlook?
questions.reference_answer: Risks are skewed to the downside: renewed escalation of hostilities or prolonged disruptions to commodity flows could raise commodity prices, intensify inflation and food insecurity, trigger financial stress and lower growth; in a severe energy-disruption scenario with financial stress, global growth could fall to 1.3 percent in 2026. Persistent trade policy uncertainty, geopolitical strains and weather-related shocks are also material risks. Upside: broader AI investment and adoption.

questions.question: How much less energy does iMac use compared to the ENERGY STAR requirement?
questions.reference_answer: iMac uses 58 percent less energy than the ENERGY STAR requirement (footnote 18: based on ENERGY STAR Program Requirements for Computers).

questions.question: What is the total carbon footprint of the iMac, and how much of that comes from product use versus manufacturing?
questions.reference_answer: Total product footprint is 346 kg CO2e for iMac (two ports) 256GB: production (manufacturing) 50 percent, product use 45 percent, transportation 5 percent, end-of-life <1 percent. The four-port 512GB configuration is 391 kg CO2e.

questions.question: What material is the iMac stand made from, and what percentage of it is recycled?
questions.reference_answer: The stand is made from aluminum, and it is 100 percent recycled aluminum.
